source_citation: JEDEC JESD79-5C LPDDR5 published interface specification (bandwidth/pin rates); JEDEC JESD235 HBM2/HBM2E published interface specification; Apple M1/M2 published die-configuration and memory figures (Apple product announcements and published silicon analyses, 2020-2022); TPU v1 published paper (Jouppi et al., ISCA 2017) for interposer/HBM topology; Intel Core Ultra 7 155U published platform figures (Intel product brief) for the integrated-GPU target; SAMSUNG/ Micron published LPDDR5x-7467 module rates.
license_or_access: public (JEDEC membership-free summaries + vendor-published figures); academic citations from peer-reviewed publications

lpddr5_unified_memory.name: LPDDR5/LPDDR5x unified-memory reference (Apple-M-class + Intel 155U class)
lpddr5_unified_memory.interface: LPDDR5 16-bit channels x N packages, LPDDR5x up to 7467 MT/s per pin

latency_ns.typical_random_access_note: end-to-end SoC load-to-use, published analyses range 80-120 ns

lpddr5_unified_memory.zero_copy_note: Apple-M-class unified memory: CPU/GPU/NPU share one physical address space; no PCIe-style DMA copy exists on the die — bandwidth is paid once per touch (cited in M1 published architecture analyses)
citations: JEDEC JESD79-5C LPDDR5 (published summary rates: 4800/6400/7467 MT/s)
Apple M1 published figures: 68.25 GB/s memory bandwidth (Apple, November 2020)
Apple M2 published figures: ~100 GB/s (Apple, June 2022)
Intel Core Ultra 7 155U: LPDDR5x-7467, 68 GB/s max (Intel product brief)

hbm_reference.name: HBM2/HBM2E interposer reference (TPU v1 topology)
hbm_reference.topology: silicon interposer connects compute die to 2-4 HBM stacks; TSV-based, ~55 µm bump pitch (published TPU v1 analyses)
citations: Jouppi et al., ISCA 2017 (TPU v1: 600 GB/s HBM)
JEDEC JESD235 HBM2: 8 Gb/s/pin x 1024-bit bus per stack

discrete_pcie_reference.name: Discrete accelerator over PCIe 4.0 x16 (copy-penalty baseline)
discrete_pcie_reference.copy_penalty: every host->device weight/activation move pays a full DMA copy; driver round-trip latency ~5-10 µs per submission (published NVIDIA/AMD driver analyses)

cache_hierarchy_reference.name: Desktop-class cache hierarchy reference (Apple-M / x86 published figures)
citations: Apple M1 published microarchitectural analyses (Anandtech, Dougadams/amd, 2020-2021); Intel 12th-gen published cache latencies

interposer_reference.name: Silicon interposer passive RDL reference
interposer_reference.rc_delay_note: interposer RDL trace RC delay is sub-ns for cm-scale routes (published EM analyses); model bus latency as 1 cycle per hop on the NoC

equations: effective_BW = peak_BW x achieved_efficiency (Roofline: operational_intensity vs min(PeakFLOPs/AI, PeakBW))
copy_time_cycles = bytes / (bytes_per_cycle) with bytes_per_cycle = BW_GBps x 1e9 / clock_Hz
zero_copy_savings_bytes = weight_bytes (weights resident in unified memory across invocations)

valid_operating_envelope.note: Interface rates are JEDEC-published maximums; achieved bandwidth is workload-dependent. The SoC Architect workspace presents all figures with the SIMULATED_ARCHITECTURAL_MODEL badge.

provenance_note: All figures above are vendor-published or JEDEC-published interface maximums and peer-reviewed analyses — no invented constants. Where a range exists in public sources, the cited published figure is used verbatim.
